Crate Engine: A 508 BHP Chevrolet 383 Stroker V8

CA
By Chloe Adams Car Culture & Restomod Editor • via Silodrome Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: Silodrome Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights
  • This is a 383 stroker V8 crate engine from the team at The Hot Rod Company, it’s rated at 508 bhp and it was developed for street-driven muscle cars, hot rods, trucks, and other automotive applications that favor plenty of torque low in the rev-range.
  • Each engine comes with a two year warranty, and they’re built in the United States by hand at the company’s 17,000 square foot facility in Washington State, not far from the Montana border.

⚡ EDITORIAL TAKE • CHLOE ADAMS Car Culture & Restomod Editor

Heritage Preservation vs Modern Performance

Automotive passion is increasingly defined by the synthesis of analog soul and contemporary engineering. This coverage from Silodrome illustrates how bespoke builders, private collectors, and restomod artists are preserving the golden eras of internal combustion while adopting carbon fiber composites and precision craftsmanship.

Big Picture: Auction hammer prices and enthusiast demand indicate sustained historical appreciation for rare, analog driver's vehicles.

This is a 383 stroker V8 crate engine from the team at The Hot Rod Company, it’s rated at 508 bhp and it was developed for street-driven muscle cars, hot rods, trucks, and other automotive applications that favor plenty of torque low in the rev-range.

📌 The Core Development

Each engine comes with a two year warranty, and they’re built in the United States by hand at the company’s 17,000 square foot facility in Washington State, not far from the Montana border.

This is the Chevrolet 383 Stroker V8 crate engine built by Hot Rod Company of Greenacres, Washington. It turns out 508 bhp and it was developed for street-driven muscle cars, hot rods, and modified trucks, with a focus on excellent low-end torque and usable performance, rather than high-rpm bragging rights.

🔍 Background & Sector Context

The Hot Rod Company is a high-performance crate engine builder based out of Spokane Valley, Washington. It specializes in small-block and LS-based Chevrolet V8s, and it was co-founded by JR and Katie Roby.

The Robys say they started the business in 2006, while budgeting for their wedding and trying to stay out of debt. JR listed an engine from one of his race cars on Craigslist for $5,000, and it sold within a day. “And the phone kept ringing and ringing,” he later recalled in a 2023 interview.

📊 Industry & Real-World Impact

He told Katie that if the calls continued he would say the engine was for sale and build another , and within the hour he said yes to the next caller. People kept calling about the original listing for days after, and it became very clear that there was an untapped market for good quality crate engines.

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

JR grew up in Salem, Oregon, where his after-school chores included stripping and building engines and transmissions with his father. He started drag racing at 16, and later while working as a personal trainer, he was sponsored by 24 Hour Fitness, which gave him a drag car and $30,000 a year to compete. He moved to Spokane in 2002 to help open one of the chain’s gyms.

The company has a policy that each engine is built by a single person, and that person signs the block when it’s done. A build takes about two days on average, but it can take longer for more complex builds. JR notes that the company has had warranty issues on fewer than 1% of their builds, a figure he credits partly to the one-builder approach.
